rounds.text: Cranex Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a calculated margin of safety of 37.0% [E43, E44]. This valuation gap is supported by a robust profit growth trajectory, which has reached 60% over the last three years and 25% over the trailing twelve months [E18, E19]. The company is benefiting from a sector tailwind in Capital Goods, which provides a favorable macro backdrop for its operations [E59, E61]. Furthermore, management confidence is evident through the increase in promoter holdings from 42.92% to 47.70% since September 2023 [E40]. While the stock has recently outperformed in terms of profit growth relative to price [E47], the current market price implies an earnings growth rate of only 11.6%, which is well below the base case assumption of 18.0% [E45]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E32, E33], a lack of dividend payouts [E4, E49], and high debtor days [E52].

Cranex Ltd trades at an attractive discount, backed by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 126 per share against its current market price of Rs 79.3, providing a substantial margin of safety of 37.0% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that today's market price only prices in an 11.6% earnings growth rate, which sits well below the base case assumption of 18.0% [E45]. Profit momentum is strong, demonstrated by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 26%, a 3-year growth of 60%, and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 25% [E17, E18, E19]. Operating margins have also structurally expanded, rising by 3 percentage points to 8% in the TTM period compared to three years prior [E28], while promoters have demonstrated confidence by increasing their holding by 4.78 percentage points to 47.70% [E40]. Additionally, the broader business benefits from a supportive macro backdrop with the Capital Goods sector in a clear tailwind with a score of +0.68 [E59, E61], and recent results show accelerating net profit growth up 33% YoY [E56, E60]. Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -1.23 Cr in Mar 2026, leading to a weak cash conversion ratio of -0.51x [E32, E33], and the company carries high debtor days of 241 days [E52].

The bull highlights a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 126 and a 37.0% margin of safety, but relies on theoretical models that clash with reality when cash flow is negative at Rs -1.23 Cr and cash conversion sits at -0.51x [E32, E33, E43, E44]. Conceded: the reverse DCF implies an 11.6% earnings growth rate against an 18.0% base case, and profit growth reads 26% over five years and 60% over three years [E17, E18, E45], yet this paper profit fails to materialize into cash while debtor days balloon to an alarming 241 days [E52]. While operating margins rose 3 percentage points to 8% [E28] and promoters increased holdings by 4.78 percentage points [E40], working capital days deteriorated heavily from 78.8 to 115 days [E53]. The bull leans on sector tailwinds with a score of +0.68 and a 33% YoY net profit acceleration [E56, E59, E60], but ignores that the company's ROCE of 10.03% and ROA of 4.18% both severely lag their sector benchmarks of 12.82% and 6.09% [E8, E10]. Finally, the 1-year share price return of -5% [E23], an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating margin trend [E30, E31], and zero dividend payout [E49] expose severe operational friction that theoretical DCF models fail to capture.
